attempts.exactPrompt:
Create one original Summonlab candidate summon portrait as a cinematic semi-realistic painted drawing. Use visible brush planes and controlled illustrative detail: not a photograph, not photoreal skin, not plastic 3D, and not cel anime. Portrait canvas 1024 x 1536. Exactly one weaponless adult, full body, three-quarter standing pose, with the entire head, both hands, both feet, hair, clothing, and all accessories fully inside a generous safe margin. Warm pale parchment studio wash, restrained warm color response, soft grounding shadow, no environmental story.

New identity Coris Vesha: 22-year-old woman, 173 cm (medium), healthy slight, narrow, long-limbed construction with low mass, skin value band-3-light-medium. Face: square compact face; asymmetric brows and broad cheek planes; crooked healed nose, balanced mouth; one brow notch. Calm closed-mouth neutral expression with no smile, grin, or theatrical acting.

Hair: red-copper-auburn, braids-twists-locs, deliberate accent: offset braid mass. Wardrobe: tailored-longcoat, specifically a cloth longcoat with a readable waist, split hem, plain underlayer, and fitted shoes; a high soft collar and uneven layered hems; bounded palette ochre-cream. Visible personal details: one small nape tattoo. Make a tattoo, scar, freckle field, or birthmark the primary recognition device. Maintenance cue: severe grooming softened by one unruly feature. Color treatment: uses the palette boldly in large blocks. Pose cue: weight settles into one heel, shoulders square, hands relaxed and completely visible. Include a wooden thread gauge only as a quiet personal object, never as a weapon.

This is ordinary but intentionally designed 1-star mortal clothing. No weapon, armor, crown, magic, aura, or glow. No affinity cue, elemental gem, floating, frame, printed star, number, UI, logo, watermark, text, extra person, duplicated anatomy, cropped extremity, or published-character resemblance. Fantasy hair colors are matte dye or pigment, never supernatural emission. Preserve plausible anatomy while allowing the declared body construction to be extreme. Do not copy the reference's person, braid, clothes, pose, palette, progression, identity, body, hair, garments, ornaments, or markings.

RESERVE ACTIVATION: This is a fresh base summon, not an edit or regeneration of any existing hero. Create the new identity described above using only the authorized rendering-style reference. Honor the complete activated physical manifest and reserve character kernel; no failed hero or failed candidate is a visual source.

findings.observation: Original-resolution inspection shows exactly one adult woman with one coherent body and no duplicated anatomy.
The entire head and hair, both relaxed hands, both fitted shoes, coat hems, thread gauge, and hanging details remain inside generous canvas margins.

Visible brush planes and simplified illustrative texture across skin, hair, cloth, and parchment establish a cinematic semi-realistic painted drawing rather than photography, plastic 3D, or cel anime.

The slight long-limbed body, square compact face, copper locs, ochre-cream tailored split longcoat, high collar, fitted shoes, and wooden thread gauge read clearly, but the required one small nape tattoo became a large side/front-neck mark; facial and arm freckling, earrings, necklace, braid cuffs, tassels, and an extra canister exceed the density-1 detail manifest.
The balanced mouth is closed and unsmiling; gaze and asymmetric brow remain controlled without theatrical acting.
The subject remains a grounded cloth-clad mortal with a quiet wooden tool and no weapon, armor, crown, magic, aura, affinity cue, glow, frame, printed star, number, UI, logo, watermark, or text.

The compact face and tailored coat differ, but the shaved-side, very long ringed braid draped over one shoulder reproduces the reference’s dominant hair silhouette and ornament construction too closely for the strict non-transfer gate.

attempts.retryReason: Strict inspection rejected manifest fidelity and original identity. The orchestrator authorized exactly one call and no correction, so no corrective attempt was made.
